Re: Limited Scope Representation — Review and Negotiation of Commercial Lease Only

Dear Mr. Doyle:

Thank you for asking us to help. This letter sets out the LIMITED scope of what we will and will not do, so there is no misunderstanding later. Please read it carefully, and do not sign it until you have.

1. WHAT WE WILL DO. We will do these things and only these things:
   (a) review the proposed commercial lease for the premises at 1400 Foundry Road, Nashville, dated March 30, 2026;
   (b) advise you in writing on its terms; and
   (c) negotiate revisions to it with the landlord's counsel on your behalf, through the execution of the lease or May 31, 2026, whichever comes first.

2. WHAT WE WILL NOT DO. We are NOT representing you in, and we will NOT be responsible for, any of the following. Each of them may matter to your business, and someone should be looking at them:
   (a) the formation, governance, or tax structure of your business;
   (b) any zoning, permitting, code-compliance, or environmental question about the premises, including whether your intended use is permitted;
   (c) any financing, guaranty, or personal-liability question, including whether to sign a personal guaranty;
   (d) any dispute, litigation, or arbitration arising from the lease, whether before or after signing;
   (e) any employment, insurance, or intellectual-property matter; and
   (f) any tax advice of any kind, including the tax treatment of tenant improvement allowances.

3. YOU REMAIN RESPONSIBLE FOR THE REST. Because this representation is limited, you are responsible for every matter outside Section 1, including watching every deadline outside it. We are not monitoring anything for you outside Section 1.

4. YOUR INFORMED CONSENT. Tennessee Rule of Professional Conduct 1.2(c) permits a lawyer to limit the scope of a representation if the limitation is reasonable under the circumstances and the client gives informed consent. By signing below you confirm that we have explained the limitation, that you have had the opportunity to ask questions about what is excluded and what could go wrong as a result, and that you consent to it. You may withdraw that consent at any time by writing to us, and we will then either expand the scope by a written amendment or end the representation.

5. FEES. Our fee is $450 per hour for partners and $275 per hour for associates, billed monthly and due within thirty (30) days. We estimate the total at $6,000 to $9,000, which is an ESTIMATE and not a cap; we will tell you promptly if it looks likely to be exceeded. You have paid an advance fee of $3,000, which we hold in our client trust account and apply to invoices as they are issued, with any unearned balance returned to you.

6. COSTS. Filing fees, courier charges, and third-party costs are billed at cost.

7. CONFLICTS. We have run a conflicts check and have found none. We represent other commercial tenants and landlords in unrelated matters, and we may continue to do so.

8. CONFIDENTIALITY. Everything you tell us in connection with this matter is confidential and privileged, and remains so after this representation ends.

9. HOW THIS ENDS. This representation ends on the earlier of the events in Section 1(c), or on written notice from either of us. We will send you a closing letter when it does. You may end it at any time and for any reason.

10. NO GUARANTEE. We have made no promise about the outcome of the negotiation, and none should be inferred.

If this letter states your understanding, please sign and return the enclosed copy.

Very truly yours,

BRIGHTWATER & OSEI LLP

/s/ Priya Osei
Priya Osei

AGREED AND ACCEPTED, with informed consent to the limited scope described above:
